About us
The Department of Global Health & Social Medicine is a unique, interdisciplinary social sciences department at King’s College London founded in 2012. Its mission is to address the changing landscape of global health and medicine through social science perspectives.
About the role
The Department invites applications for a Lecturer in Social Science and Social Theory. This is a 2-year fixed term post that will not be extended beyond the 2 years.
We welcome applicants in any area of the social sciences with an interest in the social, cultural, political and economic aspects of contemporary medicine and health. You should hold a PhD degree in the social sciences or humanities (e.g., anthropology, sociology, history, geography, political science, STS, development studies). Your areas of research might include but are not limited to: the politics of global health; drugs and culture; the politics of reproduction; racism and health; emerging infectious diseases and zoonosis; toxic environments and health; humanitarian reason; pharmaceuticalisation; structural violence; mental health and society; biopolitics; as well as other areas that relate to one of our research groups.
The successful candidate will also have proven teaching ability, expertise in enquiry-based, participatory and critical pedagogies, and a commitment to inclusive and democratic ways of working.

title: Senior Scientific Associate (Fixed Term)
description:
Join the Crossley Research Group at the Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute, where we investigate RNA-DNA hybrid molecules known as R-loops and their role in human disease. Our research focuses on understanding how R-loops contribute to genome instability and inflammation, and how these molecules and the cellular responses they trigger can be harnessed for cancer detection and treatment. To learn more about the group, visit:
https://www.cruk.cam.ac.uk/research-groups/crossley-group/
We are looking for an experienced, scientifically driven and collaborative researcher to join our growing team. This role combines hands-on experimental research with opportunities to contribute to scientific support activities and laboratory operations. You will work closely with colleagues to advance projects through to publication, help establish new research directions and methodologies, and, if desired, take the lead on your own projects. You will also partner with our Senior Scientific Associate, Dr Mawer, to support the day-to-day management and smooth running of the laboratory.
What You'll Be Doing
Working across a range of cutting-edge research projects, you will use techniques including:
Molecular biology, such as cloning, western blotting, human cell culture, CRISPR/Cas gene editing, lentiviral infection and qPCR.
RNA and nucleic acid biochemistry, including RNA/DNA and RNA-DNA hybrid isolation, immunoprecipitations and pull-down assays.
Immunofluorescence microscopy and flow cytometry.
Genomics approaches, including next-generation sequencing (NGS) library preparation and bioinformatics analysis.
About You
We are particularly interested in candidates with strong molecular biology and biochemistry expertise, alongside experience in mammalian cell and/or tissue culture. You should have in-depth knowledge in at least one of the following areas:
Genome stability
RNA biology
Chromatin biology
Innate immunity
Cancer biology
Experience with next-generation sequencing and/or bioin

Can you shape the digital transformation of one of the UK's most visited museum groups?
About us
The Science Museum Group (SMG) is a world-leading cultural organisation, welcoming millions of visitors each year to the Science Museum in London, the Science and Industry Museum in Manchester, the National Railway Museum in York, Locomotion in Shildon, and the National Science and Media Museum in Bradford.
Digital is changing how people discover culture, plan visits and connect with meaningful stories. At SMG, this creates an exciting opportunity to make our collections more accessible, relevant and engaging through audience-first digital experiences.
Over the next four years, we will bring our websites, online collections and museum experiences together into a more seamless digital journey, expanding our reach, boosting commercial resilience and building the skills and responsible AI practices needed to innovate with confidence.
We are seeking a Head of Digital Products and Experience to develop SMG's goal for a more connected digital experience across our sites. This is a full-time role (35 hours per week) and can be based at any Science Museum Group site.
The role currently works to a hybrid working pattern, which offers flexibility to work from home. There will be a requirement to travel between our sites with frequent travel to London as this is where a majority of the team sit.

About us
Royal Museums Greenwich is a collection of diverse historical sites. The sites are the National Maritime Museum, Cutty Sark, the Royal Observatory, and the Queen’s House. Each of these sites has a unique identity and a common purpose to serve our communities, through sharing our collections and expertise. We are a place to explore the sea, space, art and history, and our strategy ‘Charting Our Course’ puts people at the core of its success.
The Role
If you are passionate about the role Museums play in the learning journeys of children and young people, then this is the role for you. We are looking for a dynamic individual to work with schools and teachers to support and inspire collections-based learning at the National Maritime Museum and the Queen’s House. You will lead on the development, delivery and resourcing of historical enquiry programmes from early years to post 16, giving all school learners a high-quality experience that is unique to our sites. You will also nurture relationships with key internal and external stakeholders, ensuring that audience voice is embedded into everything we do.
The successful candidate will have a proven track record of engaging children and young people using museum collections and a great understanding of the needs of school learners and teachers. Effective time management and written and verbal presentation skills are also required. This role involves working with histories relating to empire and the transatlantic trade of enslaved people so experience of culturally sensitive approaches to exploring these topics is essential. It’s a fast-paced and rewarding role that puts learning at the centre of the Museum.
